label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
**Subject: Statement Regarding Bus 41, Route 9, Tuesday, October 27, 2026**

[Date]

Mrs. Okafor,

I received your complaint dated October 29, 2026 from my supervisor, Darlene [Last Name], on November 3. Thank you for writing it. I know it's frightening for a parent when a child doesn't get off at the stop as expected, and I understand why that afternoon was hard for you and for Amara. I'm sorry she had a bad afternoon. I want you to have my full account, and I've tried to give it to you plainly and fairly.

I have been a school bus driver for 28 years and have no prior written complaints or disciplinary actions. I take the safety of every child on my bus seriously, and Amara is no exception. I drive her every day, and I care about her.

**What happened**

On Tuesday, October 27, I was running the afternoon route on Bus 41. I arrived at the stop at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street at 3:52 p.m. The schedule calls for 3:50, so I was two minutes behind. Amara has a green tag on her backpack, which under district policy means an adult must be present at the stop to receive her. I waited at the stop until about 3:55. I looked at the corner for the full wait and did not see an adult.

At 3:56 I radioed dispatch. Dispatch contacted Fairmont Elementary. Under the district procedure for kindergarten riders, when no adult is present, the student stays on the bus and returns to school, and the school contacts the parent. That is what I did. I completed the rest of the route with Amara on board, and we arrived back at Fairmont at 4:31 p.m. I walked her into the office myself and handed her to Mrs. Petrakis.

**Your account**

You've told the office that you were parked across Brandt Street by the laundromat and waved to me. I am not doubting that you were there. I want to be honest that I did not see you. A box truck was parked on that side of the street, and I did not see a car or a person waving. If I had seen you, I would have responded and I would have understood what was happening. I know that is hard to hear, and I'm sorry it went the way it did.

You also told the office I drove away laughing. I was not laughing. As we pulled out, a fourth grader in seat two had gotten out of her seat, and I was telling her to sit back down. I understand how that may have looked from across the street, and I'm sorry it appeared that way to you.

**How Amara was**

Amara was calm and safe the entire time. She was coloring on her folder, and she asked if she could keep riding. I told her we were going on a little extra trip, because I did not want her to be upset while we sorted things out. I'm glad she was not frightened on the bus, and I believe that matters for how the afternoon should be understood.

**Following the policy**

I want to be clear that I followed the district rule for a kindergarten rider with a green tag and no adult at the stop. I am not able to leave the bus unattended at a stop, and I am not able to leave fourteen other students on board to go look for an adult across the road. The rule exists so that a five-year-old is never released to an empty corner, and I would have been failing her and the other children if I had set it aside. I am not sorry for following that rule, but I am sorry for the fear and worry it caused you.

**Requests**

1. Please pull the camera footage from Bus 41 for the stop at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street on October 27, approximately 3:50 to 3:57 p.m. It should show the corner, the approach to the stop, and whether an adult was present.

2. In the future, if you plan to meet Amara at the stop, please let the school or dispatch know ahead of time. When you are there, please stand on the bus side of the street, or step out of your car where I can see you. That way I can confirm an adult is present before the doors open.

3. Please contact the transportation office or dispatch before the next pickup so we can confirm the arrangement together.

**Closing**

I am glad to keep driving Amara, and I want this resolved in a way that keeps her safe and keeps the lines of communication open between us. I have grandchildren of my own, so I understand how much you care about your daughter, and I would like to work with you to make sure she gets home safely every day.

Thank you for reading this. If you have questions, you can reach me through the transportation office.

Sincerely,

[Your Full Name]
School Bus Driver, Bus 41, Route 9
[Employee ID]
[Phone or contact through transportation office]

---

**A few notes before you send it:**

- **Footage:** The bus camera may not show across the street or the laundromat side. The request is still worth making, but don't count on it proving her version or yours.
- **Dates and times:** I used the times you gave me. Check them against your run sheet or dispatch log before it goes in the file.
- **Left out:** I didn't mention the earlier incident on your route with another family. It's a different situation, and it could read as deflecting.
- **Tone:** The "step out of your car" request reads as a safety request, but it could still sound directive to her. If you want it softer, you could drop "step out of your car" and keep "let the school or dispatch know ahead of time."
- **Before Friday, November 13:** Check with Darlene whether the district wants a specific format, signature block, or delivery method, since this goes both to the file and to Mrs. Okafor.
